description: cost-ledger (ADR 0031, ADR 0025): the golden rows behind the `llm_call` ledger, and the one part of that row both tiers already speak. **`llm_call` has no table.** No migration creates it, nothing writes it, and no boundary schema is generated from it — so this file records the row ADR 0025's amendment of 05/09/2026 fixes, written down once rather than twice, and describes nothing the database has. What waits for the migration that brings the table: the writer, ADR 0025's retention — six months of rows, then a monthly per-workspace aggregate — ADR 0028's boundary schema generated from the table, and the five assertions ADR 0028 makes over `boundarySchemas` to hold a refinement to its column. None of them can be asserted against a table that does not exist, and a fixture that asserted them would be asserting its own bytes, which is the failure ADR 0031's redaction amendment names. What is held is the purposes. `purpose` is the one field of this row whose vocabulary is already live in both tiers: the api's `LLM_PURPOSES` over the schema's `llm_purpose` enum (packages/core/src/llm/index.ts, packages/schema/src/schema.ts), and, in the worker, the purpose it seeds a route with and resolves one by, `llm_route_for(purpose)` casting to that same enum. Each suite reads the purposes these rows use and holds them to its own tier's, both ways, so a purpose added to a tier and not to these rows — or to these rows and not to a tier — is that tier's red suite. Neither suite reads the other tier's list and neither writes the purposes out itself. Everything else here is recorded rather than held. `fields` is the row ADR 0025 names, one entry per column, and every row carries exactly those keys and no others: that is how *never the prompt or the completion* is checked against the disk rather than left to a reader, because a row cannot carry what the field set does not name and the field set names nothing that could hold either. `outcomes` is the words `outcome` takes; they are this file's own, for the migration to settle, and each is behind at least one row so neither is a word with nothing under it. A row names the run or the answer it served under two nullable columns with exactly one of them set, because a run and an answer are separate records and one foreign key cannot point at both. `cost_usd` carries its unit in its name and its value as a decimal string: money is not a float, the column will be `numeric`, and dollars are what a provider prices a call in — converting that to what a workspace is billed is a signal's work and never the row's. `seconds` is wall-clock, ADR 0025's own word for it. The rows are six across two workspaces: one per purpose, and one whose outcome is a failure. Two carry `tokens_out` 0 — the embedding call, which has no output tokens at all, and the failed answering call, which produced none — so no reader can take a zero for a failure, the outcome word being the only thing that says so, and the failed row still carries a cost because the tokens it sent were spent. The figures are one plausible day's calls and no suite asserts a number among them; nothing seeds these rows, there being nothing yet to seed them into.

fields.is: the workspace whose spend this call is, and the column every signal over this ledger groups by
what the call was for, from the vocabulary both tiers hold these rows to
the `llm_route` row the call was resolved through, so spend can be read back per route
the model actually called, beside the route because a route's model is edited and a row is not
tokens sent, which are spent whatever the call returns
tokens returned, zero where a call returns none and zero where it fails
wall-clock time the call took, the figure the onboarding ETA is read off
what the call cost at the provider's price, a decimal string because money is not a float
the run this call served, null where it served an answer
the answer this call served, null where it served a run

outcomes.is: the call returned, and its tokens, seconds and cost are what it spent doing so
the call returned nothing the caller could use — refused, cut off or timed out — and what it spent before that is still spent
